title: Korba coal mining & washeries: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Coal mining in Korba is opencast, transport-heavy work; washeries turn raw coal into washed coal and rejects, and cash is made on yield and ash reduction.** The district page says coal is abundant, SECL has important mines in Korba and four thermal plants generate 3650 MW [4]. The official washery list shows KJSL Coal & Power at Dhatura, Pali, Korba with 4.10 capacity, non-coking, private [3]. The local project tracker shows 78 mining projects in Chhattisgarh worth ₹0.92 lakh crore, 28 above ₹100 Cr, 7 added in the last 30 days [1]; the Korba Manikpur opencast expansion is from 3.50 to 5.25 MTPA [1]. **Korba-specific washery financials are thin in these sources, so underwrite from first principles and peer prints; the official data pack returns UNKNOWN, with no score [D].**

## Where value and cash sit
**The washery earns on yield and ash reduction, not on the coal price line alone.** Inputs are raw coal, transport, water and power, consumables, land and EC; cash goes out for raw coal and transport before washed coal is collected, and rejects can absorb cash if disposal is slow. Pricing power is weak on FSA/linkage coal and volatile on e-auction. Peer results and a broker/rating note show CIL Q2FY27 e-auction premium at 51% versus 57%, e-auction realisations at Rs 2,283/t, FSA at Rs 1,510/t up 4% [6]; SAIL’s imported coking coal at ₹22,930/t rose ₹1,700 QoQ and OPM compressed to 12.9% [5]. **So when a proposal lands, check raw-coal tie-up, yield, reject sale and receivable ageing before the projected price; if the yield, ash content, landed raw-coal cost or reject price is missing, write ‘collect from customer’.**

## What has changed now
**Local project activity is real, but peer results show price and margin volatility, not a clean upward cycle.** The tracker lists new washeries in Janjgir Champa at 1440000 MT, Bilaspur at 0.99 MTPA and Rs.150 Million, plus the Manikpur expansion [1]. CIL volume is strong: Q2FY27 production 151 MT up 4% and offtake 186 MT up 12–13% [6]. SAIL cut FY27 volume guidance to 21 MT from 22 MT after the coal miss [5]. Old local press reports Balco shut its Korba rolling mill with around 1,000 jobs and later planned to resume [2]; that article is old, but it warns that Korba industrial demand can swing. **Treat the pipeline as a reason to select borrowers, not to loosen credit.**

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue private non-coking washeries with EC, firm raw-coal linkage and more than one offtake buyer; avoid borrowers whose cash depends on one mine allotment or coal trading.** The official list shows private washeries in the 0.90 to 5.00 capacity band [3], and the pipeline has new washeries at 0.99 MTPA and 1440000 MT [1]. Good targets are existing operators adding a unit, SECL contractors with owned equipment and work orders, and transport firms with dispatch evidence. Avoid new coal traders, single-reject-buyer washeries, borrowers without EC, and industrial exposures that rely on Balco-type demand without a contract.

## How to grow safely
**Structure to the cash cycle: secured working capital against coal stock and receivables, escrow of sale proceeds, and covenants set from customer data.** Take every month stock and yield statements, GST returns, e-way bills, sales register, raw-coal allotment, reject sale invoices, receivable ageing and transport bills. Set covenants on yield, stock cover, receivable ageing, DSCR and promoter contribution; keep EC and lease documents on file. For capex, match tenor to washery ramp and require completion benchmarks. **Where a figure is missing, write ‘collect from customer’ and do not fill it with an estimate.**

## Early warning
**The first sign is cash moving into stock and rejects while dispatches slow.** Watch yield reports against the sanctioned base, reject inventory without sale invoices, top-buyer ageing, linkage or e-auction expiry, and mismatch between GST sales and e-way bills. If a borrower asks for enhancement while stock rises and receivables age, ask for buyer confirmation and re-price to a lower drawing power. **A washery that cannot show monthly reject sales and buyer-wise ageing is not bankable at normal limits.**
watch: Washed coal yield falls below the sanctioned base or reject stock rises without sale invoices -> cut drawing power and ask for buyer-wise offtake proof.
GST returns and e-way bills vs sales register (monthly)
Dispatch value lags invoiced sales or e-way bills do not match -> stop enhancement and reconcile before fresh limits.
Allotment expires, is diverted or is only verbal -> freeze limit and re-rate to tolling-only exposure.
Top-buyer ageing crosses the sanctioned bucket -> seek buyer confirmation, re-price drawing power, and shift to escrow.
Peer e-auction premium and washed-coal price (monthly)
Premium falls below the Q2FY27 51% print or washed-coal price falls below base case -> rework covenants and reduce unsecured exposure.
